value.assumption_check: The unstated load-bearing assumption is a VALUE one, not a technical one: that a second agent's suspicions are worth ~6GB of a 15GB box. Nothing measures that, and the honest consequence is that the device must be instrumented for its conversion rate (suspicion to a sieve that fires) from the first day rather than after it has earned goodwill. A second assumption: that hermes' ledgers are tailable as an append-only stream — measured that skill_ledger writes JSONL with content-addressed manifests, NOT measured that it flushes in a way a tail can follow.
value.builder_check: (1) WHERE: cairn/devices/hermes/0/ — device rung, instance 0, never a singleton exemption. (2) WHAT IT MAY NOT DO, and this needs to be physics not prose: it may not write a gate passage, may not seal a validation, may not appear in any charter's gated_by. A builder should ask how that is ENFORCED rather than declared; the honest first answer is that it holds no credential the doors accept, which is enforcement by Law 6 rather than by a check. (3) ITS INFERENCE: points at the OpenAI door (sibling ticket), which means THIS TICKET DEPENDS ON THAT ONE and should read queued on it rather than racing it. (4) ITS LEDGERS: tail skill_ledger.jsonl and the curator ledger into the device trail via cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py — compose the floor, do not author a receiver. (5) WHAT NOT TO BUILD: no poller, no scheduler on the Cairn side, no supervisor. (6) INSTALL: hermes ships a curl-pipe-bash installer from its own domain; run it in the constrained box and keep it away from ~/.cairn and both git roots on first run.
value.collision_check: Checked 'reaching for daemons is drift' — a DISTINCTION, and the whys separate cleanly. CLAUDE.md defines a device as a top-level thing that is ITS OWN PROCESS, so a long-lived hermes process is the rung's normal shape; the drift would be CAIRN growing a poller to watch it, and that is a bound for the charter. Checked Law 8 (peers require proof first): not a collision but a CONSTRAINT this ticket inherits — 3,977 upstream tests buy nothing here, and it grafts one ticket at a time. Checked 'nothing in inspectors or gates is allowed to be llm': not a collision because the role explicitly passes no gate, and that must be physics rather than manners.
value.falsifier_check: The intent's falsifier stands with one clause carrying the weight: it has filed at least one trouble or question CC did not raise. That is what distinguishes a running process from a peer, and it is why 'it starts' is explicitly not enough — aider_shim can already claim that and has 0 surviving edits. HORIZON: one week of running alongside CC. Wrong-intent tells are both written: needing to fork after all, and suspicions nobody converts. MEASURED RELOCATION CLAUSE rather than a kill: 15GB total, ~9GB available, CC has OOM-killed this box three times at 12-14GB; if they cannot coexist the device moves to Hex.
value.missing_check: Yes. 'Files questions and troubles' was asserted wrapped and is not: BOTH of those are doors with contracts, and whether a non-CC hand may fire them is an open Law 6 question. The trouble door and the question corpus each have an owner, and hermes is not in any gated_by list anywhere. This is the ticket's real edge and it is written here rather than discovered at BUILDME: hermes' output may have to land as a PROPOSAL that CC or Akien admits, not as a direct write.

value.better_approach: (a) Fork and instrument inside — rejected on measurement: 922MB of .git, upstream at PR #107,000, so every pull becomes a merge, in order to obtain logging that inference_domain has produced since 2026-08-18 (one emission line per call carrying host, path, model, provider and the route walked). (b) Run it with no integration and read its files by hand — rejected because that is exactly the unmeasured state Akien named this morning as the 'working on myself' problem; an antagonist nobody can audit is a second voice, not a second measurement.
value.hidden_assumption: That a second agent's suspicions are worth 6GB of a 15GB box. Unmeasured. The number that would settle it is the conversion rate from hermes suspicion to a deterministic sieve that actually fires, and nothing measures that yet — which makes it the first thing the device should be instrumented for, not the last.
value.prior_art: aider_shim is the standing prior art and it is a WARNING, not an endorsement: a third-party coding agent already wrapped as a Cairn device, with the standing thread recording 0 surviving edits from it. That is evidence about how hard the shim pattern is, and it is why this intent's falsifier demands a FILED TROUBLE rather than a running process — 'it starts' is what aider_shim can already claim.
value.real_collision: With the standing rule 'reaching for daemons is drift': hermes runs a gateway process, watchdogs and a periodic scheduler. NOT terminal, and the whys differ. A DEVICE is by CLAUDE.md's own definition a top-level thing that is its own process, so a long-lived hermes process is the rung's normal shape. The drift would be CAIRN growing a poller to watch it — and that is a bound to write into the charter, not a reason to refuse.

value.FOR_THE_CHARTER: The device charter should name the approvals shape we run hermes under rather than inheriting a default. CC's read, NOT ruled: mode manual or off, with the real constraints written as deterministic globs in approvals.deny -- because a glob list is checkable and a guardian prompt is not. Akien is the arbiter.
value.THE_SCOPE: AI inside a device is the NORM in Cairn, not an exception needing a case made. CC, aider, the librarian and the embeddings generator are all AI-in-a-device. The rule 'nothing in inspectors or gates is allowed to be llm' targets the FIRE-PATH TIER ONLY -- Cairn's own inspectors, sieves and gates, where a verdict must be replayable. hermes' internal approval cognition is not one of our gates. Akien remains the arbiter of where AI is OK, per device; that is his judgment to make, not a prohibition for CC to enforce.
value.WHAT_ACTUALLY_GOVERNS_HERMES_ADVANCING_A: Our doors, unchanged and indifferent to whose hand fires them. A crossing rides cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit; the BUILDME entry gate demands a berthed validate packet claiming the ticket, an intent_berth and a sorted_berth; the PROVED exit gate demands a complete passing verdict artifact with instrument and evidence per criterion; proofs seal under the tester. hermes cannot write a crossing -- Akien's standing rule is that only a deterministic gate or an explicit word from him creates one. So 'he does it our way' is already physics for the parts that matter, and the double-checking Akien names is the layer above that.
value._why: CC read hermes' built-in approval cognition as a collision with Akien's standing rule and raised it to his gate. It is not one. Recorded here so the device charter is written from the corrected scope, not from the mistake.
